title: Criminology, B.A. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Pre-First-Year/Second-Year-Seminar curriculum, built from the archived 2022-23 bulletin's own Suggested Academic Plan and Program Requirements tabs (fetched directly this pass). Confirmed structurally identical through 2023-24 and 2024-25 (see CRIM-2023.json / CRIM-2024.json's own notes) -- the 121-credit, no-LA-83/no-LA-283 curriculum was replaced starting with the 2025-26 edition (see CRIM-2025.json / CRIM-2026.json), which added LA 83 (First-Year Seminar, 1.5 cr) and LA 283 (Second-Year Seminar, 1.5 cr) and raised the total to 124 credits. Entrance to major requires a 2.00 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly (matches CRIM-2026.json's own convention). Real gap this year's archive shares with 2026's: STAT 200's real prereq_groups require MATH 21, which needs MATH 4, which needs MATH 3 -- none of these appear anywhere in the bulletin's own suggested plan for any year checked, so (mirroring CRIM-2026.json's own fix for the identical gap) MATH 3 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 21 were added explicitly across Semesters 1-3, each swapped in for a generic Gen Ed slot the bulletin's own plan already carried that semester (GQ in Semester 1, a generic Gen Ed in Semester 2, a generic Gen Ed in Semester 3) so semester credit totals stay faithful to the bulletin while the real prereq chain becomes schedulable; the simulator naturally defers STAT 200 (kept in its real bulletin position, Semester 2) to the term it actually becomes eligible, same behavior as CRIM-2026.json. The archived page's own B.A. Degree Requirements heading still said 'Foreign Language' this year (later renamed 'World Language' university-wide), but its own Suggested Academic Plan table already used 'World Language' for the actual course slots, so no plan-content change was needed for that terminology lag. The 'BA Other Cultures' slot label matches this year's and 2023-24's own bulletin wording exactly (renamed 'BA World Cultures' starting with the 2024-25 edition -- see CRIM-2024.json). Race/Ethnicity/Gender and 4XX CRIM Core course lists are reused verbatim from CRIM-2026.json's own department-checksheet-sourced match patterns: every archived bulletin page checked (2022-23 through 2025-26) names these only as generic 'from list' categories on the program page itself, without publishing the list content there, so there is no year-specific bulletin list to verify against -- flagged here as an inherited assumption, not independently re-verified for 2022-23. CRIM 249/CRIM 250W's own prereq_groups being empty in the shared crim_catalog.json is a catalog-level (not degree-plan-year-specific) gap already flagged in CRIM-2026.json's own notes and left alone there for the same reason here: catalogs/*.json is out of scope for a degree-plan-year fix.
